The OCR layer is complete; its errors ('Zxecuttve Orbe?' for the heading, 'Ollice' for 'Office', 'provisionls', '1J25' for 1925) and the trailing noise (the printer's imprint at the foot of the page) do not affect the operative words. As an experiment and not as a precedent, and in lieu of the orders usually issued making four hours a day's work on December 24 and December 31, it closes the executive departments and independent establishments in the District of Columbia, including the Government Printing Office and the Navy Yard and stations, on Saturday, December 26, 1925, and excuses federal employees in the District from duty that day, except those excepted for special public reasons or whose absence would conflict with existing law. The order gives no half-day on December 24 or December 31; its reference to the usual orders explains what it replaces and commands nothing for those days. First end: by its own terms at the close of 1925-12-26, the only day it governs. A reader who dates cessation to the first day without effect would write 1925-12-27; this claim records 1925-12-26, the day through whose end the order ran, consistent with the owner's inclusive reading of stated dates. Identity: the census register lists EO 4354 with the year only; the date December 11, 1925 and the number come from the scan.

Nothing names EO 4354. The machine USC and eCFR searches (complete, 0 hits) exclude a current-law reference; the OFR catalog search starts in 1937 and is not relied on alone.
scope_check: Whole order is one clause governing one day. No partial event is held or found.
independent_command_check: The closing and the excusal from duty are one command for one day. The words 'As an experiment, not as a precedent, in lieu of the orders heretofore usually issued' command no one: they state why the order is made and what it replaces, and have no operation once the day has passed, so they are not a retained independent command.

James from Compulsory Retirement for Age', date 1933-02-17, text_sha256 equal to the held file's) agrees in substance. EO 6030 (February 17, 1933, Herbert Hoover) exempts Charles J.
